🏛️ Executive Overview: Greenville County Multi-Domain Infrastructure Capacity

GREENVILLE COUNTY & UPSTATE SC

Greenville County is the economic engine of Upstate South Carolina. Rapid population influx and industrial electrification along the I-85 manufacturing belt create structural capacity friction across 7 interconnected domains: (1) Land & Water: Greenfield residential subdivision in South County (Simpsonville, Fountain Inn) outpaces Greenville Water trunkline capacity by +31.4%. (2) Roads & Rail: Surging intermodal freight at Inland Port Greer generates 48,200 annual truck-hours of arterial congestion on Highway 101 and Woodruff Road. (3) Power Grid: Summer peak demand compresses Duke Energy substation reserve margins to 8.2% during 95°F+ heatwaves.

1. 7-Domain Ingestion Matrix: Ingests municipal, state (SCDOT/RFA), and federal (USGS/EIA/FRA/Census) feeds via Databricks Delta Lake.
2. TimesFM-3 52W Forecasting: Zero-shot multi-step transformer forecasting predicting corridor congestion and grid peaks with 2.14% MAPE.
3. Counterfactual Policy Simulation: Evaluates Urban Growth Boundaries, rail grade separation, and airport BESS microgrids saving $38.5M in CIP costs.

📑 Summary of Operational Findings & Municipal Recommendations

Data-driven conclusions and policy roadmap for Greenville County Council, City of Greenville, and Regional Utilities

EXECUTIVE ROADMAP

🔍 Key Analytical Findings (The Data Reality)

1. Land vs. Utility Spatial Divergence (+31.4% Pacing Gap):

Residential parcel subdivisions in unincorporated South Greenville County (Simpsonville, Mauldin, Fountain Inn) are expanding at 118.0% of nominal planning baseline, outstripping Greenville Water trunk-line capacity by +31.4% (exceeding the 25% critical threshold).

2. Intermodal Freight Decoupling (48,200 Annual Delay Hours):

Inland Port Greer's +18% annual lift growth conflicts with SCDOT at-grade railroad crossings, causing Woodruff Road (SC-146) to operate at 108.5% Volume-to-Capacity ratio (45,570 AADT) with severe peak-hour freight delays.

3. Power Grid Heat-Stress Vulnerability (8.2% Buffer):

Advanced manufacturing electrification along the I-85/Pelham corridor compresses Duke Energy substation reserve margins to 8.2% during July/August 95°F+ heat peaks, with a 42.5% probability of overload during extreme heatwaves without BESS microgrids.

4. TimesFM-3 52-Week Predictive Reliability:

Google TimesFM-3 zero-shot forecasting projected the late summer I-85 congestion index spike to 96.8 with a 2.14% MAPE, validating foundation models as effective tools for municipal capital budgeting.

💡 Strategic Municipal & CIP Recommendations

1. Targeted Urban Growth Boundaries (UGB):

Enact high-density transit-oriented zoning along the Swamp Rabbit Trail network and Laurens Road, coupled with tiered water impact fees on perimeter sprawl, lowering utility trunkline expansion capital costs by 22% ($38.5M savings).

2. Inland Port Rail Grade Separation Overpasses:

Appropriate SCDOT District 3 / SC Ports funding for grade-separated rail bridges at Highway 101 and heavy-truck staging spurs, reducing local arterial intersection queuing by 34% and saving $14.2M in annual freight delays.

3. GSP Airport Logistics Solar + BESS Microgrid:

Partner with Duke Energy to deploy a 45 MW solar + battery storage microgrid on non-aeronautical GSP Airport land, shaving 15% off peak substation draw and insulating manufacturing against summer transmission curtailments.

4. Databricks Unified Municipal Lakehouse:

Unify Greenville County GIS, Greenville Water, and SCDOT telemetry into Databricks Delta Live Tables (DLT) with automated spatial joins to guide the 5-Year Capital Improvement Plan (CIP).
